key_insight: A two-level encoding in multi-spin molecules can suppress dominant dephasing first and then correct remaining off-diagonal errors, making fault-tolerant quantum computing more realistic for molecular spins.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical hardware path for quantum error correction by exploiting chemically engineered multi-spin molecules and the natural separation between dephasing and relaxation errors.
method: Use a dephasing-tolerant first-level encoding to strongly reduce pure dephasing.
Embed the protected unit into a multi-spin molecular code to handle residual off-diagonal errors.
Leverage synthetic control of molecule structure to match code properties to molecular spin physics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical demonstrations that the hybrid strategy can perform well even with only a limited number of spins per logical unit.
watch_item: The approach depends on strong error hierarchy and precise molecular engineering, so performance may degrade if dephasing is not sufficiently dominant or if the spin architecture is hard to realize experimentally.
paper_title: Beyond Pure Dephasing: Quantum Error Correction in Single Molecules Requires Multiple Spins
